plan: [ This auction is strategically equivalent to a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest exit price. With independent private values, the dominant strategy is truthful bidding to maximize expected profit. Overbidding risks winning at a loss; underbidding risks missing profitable wins. There is no multi-round learning advantage here (single round). Therefore, I will bid my value exactly: $15, ensuring I win whenever the second-highest bid is below 15 and pay that (profitable) price. ]

[ This mechanism is strategically equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the highest bid wins and pays the second-highest bid. With independent private values and risk neutrality, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. There’s no prior-round history to exploit. Avoid overbidding (risk losses) and underbidding (risk unnecessary loss). Bid 36. ]

[ This is strategically equivalent to a second‑price auction: the ascending clock ends at the second‑highest sealed bid, which is the price paid by the winner. With independent private values and risk neutrality, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value to maximize expected profit. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With one round and no history to exploit, bid exactly 42 to ensure efficient allocation and maximize expected payoff. ]
